implementation_review: The complete original 68,394-edge namespace is reconstructed, and each triangle's literal selector and edge IDs are checked against the accepted original domain.

Every pattern preserves both families' three pair minors and determinant; singleton minors are stored once per triangle. The complete 111 value and proper minors are replayed against the accepted negative record.
Full literal terms and both bounds determine row identity. Every cube origin, minimality witness, pattern table and one explicit triangle-cover dominator are retained.
Counters require 86,640 patterns, 173,280 matrices and 1,212,960 principal minors. Limits cap cube origins and unique rows at 32,490.

Errors and incomplete prefixes retain a nonaccepted status. Main acceptance must require complete=true and successful finalization with the actual serialized-byte and elapsed-time values within the declared limits.
input_authority_review: Fetched and SHA256-checked actual parent forward, complete cold and cold configuration. Their status/schema/source/configuration contracts match the loader, including the complete 1,179,048-triangle universe and the 10,830-entry ordered negative list.

Actual parent count-object key order agrees, so the source's strict JSON count comparison is valid for these frozen inputs. The cold's forward/domain/kernel/audit binding field names match the exact configuration.

The loader hash-checks every configured source, text input, compressed archive and decompressed raw input, then binds primitive kernels to both the independent full-core audit and the accepted parent census.
No old zero, prism or path cut is used to determine PSD compatibility, and all 10,830 negative triangles are retained before classification.
mathematical_review: A selected triple's three singleton, three pair and full determinant principal minors are computed with BigInt in both families. A pattern is compatible only when all fourteen minors are nonnegative.

Every positive-only partial assignment contains 111. The accepted full parent cold has no negative proper minor and lists every negative 111 determinant, so these 10,830 triples contain every PSD-only positive cube in the declared disjoint-signature eligible universe.

A positive cube is forbidden exactly when every edge-pattern completion is incompatible. One-bit removal witnesses certify minimality; the complete antichain has at most three members on three edge variables.

An isolated vertex not incident to a positive fixed edge retains its selector guard. Zero positive edges give a selector-triple cover; one positive edge gives an edge-plus-third-selector cover; three positive edges give the triangle cover.

For two positive edges, endpoint activation justifies the homogeneous path row with the shared center selector. Its lower endpoint -1 is automatic. The other row kinds contain nonnegative terms and correctly use lower endpoint zero.

The source symbolically adds nonnegative integer combinations of the retained cut and existing endpoint/bound rows to obtain the original triangle cover, with scale two in the selector-only case. This proves continuous-relaxation dominance, not merely Boolean implication.
Positive-only cubes are not claimed to cover all incompatible patterns. PSD-compatible patterns are not claimed to extend to graph embeddings.
